quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What effect does shifting to a lower gear have?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have a manual transmission. When you shift to a lower gear, it slows you down.

questions.question: How long does a pre-ride inspection take, and when should you do it?

options.text: A few minutes, once a month.
A few minutes, before every ride.
Over an hour, done by a mechanic.
Over an hour, only when carrying a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: A few minutes, before every ride.
questions.explanation: Do a thorough pre-ride inspection before every ride. It takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: If you wait one hour per alcoholic drink before riding, what is true?

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
You may still have side effects from the alcohol.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may still have side effects from the alcohol.
questions.explanation: Your body eliminates about one drink per hour on average. However, alcohol can still build up in your system even if you have only one drink per hour. This buildup can still affect your riding ability.

questions.question: Which clothing item is NOT a good choice for riding?

options.text: A jacket and pants that fully cover your arms and legs.
Boots or shoes that cover your ankles.

questions.explanation: For protection, wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high and sturdy boots or shoes that cover your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: How noticeable is a motorcycle's brake light compared to a car's?
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is usually not as noticeable as a car's brake lights. Flash your brake light before you slow down or stop to help other drivers see you.

questions.question: What is true about riding at night?

options.text: Wearing reflective clothing makes it safer.
It is not safe because drivers cannot see your turn signals.
You should only ride at night in the city.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing reflective clothing makes it safer.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective clothing at night so other drivers can see you better.

questions.question: When should a rider use their mirrors?

options.text: When slowing down or stopping suddenly.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when slowing down or stopping, when stopped at an intersection, when changing lanes, and when turning.

questions.question: Motorcycles have blind spots like cars. When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and check your blind spot.
Slow down so vehicles in your blind spot can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What does maintaining space between your motorcycle and other vehicles do?

options.text: Gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
Keeps you in one area of the lane, limiting your movement.
Allows you to rely on others to identify hazards.
Requires you to go faster to stay with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your motorcycle gives you time and room to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: How much maintenance does a motorcycle need?

options.text: Less frequent attention than a car.
More frequent attention than a car.

questions.correctAnswerText: More frequent attention than a car.
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more serious than on a car. Check your motorcycle thoroughly before every ride.

questions.question: What color are warning signs?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What happens when you drink alcohol quickly?

options.text: The more the alcohol will accumulate in your body.
The faster the alcohol is removed from your body.
The more minimal the effects of the alcohol will be.
The more likely you will be able to evade being pulled over.

questions.correctAnswerText: The more the alcohol will accumulate in your body.
questions.explanation: When you drink quickly, alcohol builds up in your body. Never drive after drinking alcohol.

questions.question: What should you do to prevent accidents?

options.text: Follow the vehicle in front of you as closely as possible.
Not look ahead and focus only on your controls.
Communicate your intentions to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate your intentions to other drivers.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, let other drivers know what you plan to do. Use your signals, brake lights, and correct lane position. Stay alert to what is ahead, behind, and next to you.

questions.question: What should you wear to help other drivers see you?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors so other drivers can see you during the day and at night.

questions.question: How can you reduce your crash risk?

options.text: Communicate your intentions to other road users.
Ride in the parts of a lane that make it difficult to be seen.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate your intentions to other road users.
questions.explanation: Make sure other drivers can see you. Use your signals, brake lights, and correct lane position. Look ahead and stay alert.

questions.question: How should a helmet fit?
questions.explanation: Your helmet should fit snugly all around your head. It must meet DOT and state standards and have no defects.

questions.question: What should you wear when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Not wear a jacket if it's warm out.
Always wear a jacket, even if it's warm out.
Not be concerned about long shoelaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always wear a jacket, even if it's warm out.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket, even in warm weather. It protects you and helps prevent dehydration. Also wear long pants and tuck in your shoelaces.

questions.question: What is most important when choosing a helmet?
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT and state standards. It should fit snugly and be free of defects.

questions.question: Before riding, which check is NOT necessary?

options.text: Trying both brake controls to ensure the brake light activates.
Ensuring that the paint is not scratched.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ensuring that the paint is not scratched.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tire pressure and condition. Check oil and fluid levels. Test the headlight, taillight, signal lights, and brake light.

questions.question: The Motorcycle Safety Foundation recommends the SEE strategy. What does "S" stand for?
questions.explanation: The SEE strategy stands for Search, Evaluate, and Execute. This helps riders make safe decisions.

questions.question: When should you use a turn signal?
questions.explanation: Use a turn signal every time you turn or change lanes. Do this even if you think no one is watching.

questions.question: Someone is tailgating you. What should you do?

options.text: Drive faster to get away from them.

questions.explanation: The safest way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. Change lanes safely and allow them to go ahead. Driving faster only makes it more dangerous by causing them to tailgate at a higher speed.

questions.question: How does a three-wheeled motorcycle handle curves?

options.text: The same as a two-wheeled motorcycle.
It should not be used in curves.
It should use the shoulder for curves.

questions.explanation: A three-wheeled motorcycle or one with a sidecar corners differently than a regular two-wheeled motorcycle.

questions.question: What happens with long-term wind noise exposure?

options.text: It is safer than listening to music.

questions.explanation: Long-term wind noise while riding can hurt your hearing, even with a helmet. Wear hearing protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: When preparing to pass, ride in the left portion of your lane because:

options.text: You cannot see the vehicle ahead.
It helps the other driver go faster.

questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass. This helps you see better and makes you more visible to drivers in the passing lane.
